candidates.title: Synthetic voter models migrating toward consumer modeling
candidates.shift: Reports describe organizations building AI models that simulate American voters to test political messaging at scale — a synthetic-population simulation capability with obvious adjacent uses.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative and off-map: if adversarial-scale persona simulation matures, similar techniques could migrate into retail site-selection, demand forecasting, or hyper-targeted in-store personalization — an unsettling extension of demographic modeling into physical retail decisions.
candidates.evidence: Independent reporting (Substack/Twitter) claiming Chinese organizations are building AI models of American voters to pre-test messaging; unverified, low credibility.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of population-scale AI simulation moving from political to potentially commercial use; if it matures, it could give real-estate and retail planners synthetic 'consumer twins' for site and format decisions, raising new ethical and regulatory questions.

candidates.title: Same-day-cycle micro-bakery format
candidates.shift: A Seoul neighborhood bakery is designed explicitly around a same-day bake-and-sell cycle in a tiny footprint, reflecting hyper-local, freshness-driven small-format food retail.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, single instance: could be an early edge of micro-footprint experiential food retail replacing larger formats in dense Asian urban markets, relevant to the People/Community branch (food & connection).
candidates.evidence: Achime Bagel Store in Munjeong-dong, Seoul, designed around a single-day production/sale cycle in a compact space.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of format shrinkage driven by freshness and locality rather than scale efficiency; if it spreads, it would push retail real estate toward smaller, higher-frequency-turnover footprints in dense urban cores.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Craft-material pop-up as luxury retail differentiator
candidates.shift: A luxury brand's mall pop-up in São Paulo is wrapped in a hand-woven wicker skin referencing local craft, rather than a standardized global store kit.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, single instance: peripheral geography (Brazil) setting an experiential-retail material standard rather than importing one — a possible edge of localized, craft-driven pop-up formats in emerging luxury markets.
candidates.evidence: Estúdio Campana's woven wicker-clad Tiffany & Co pop-up at JK Iguatemi Mall, São Paulo.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of temporary retail architecture shifting from standardized global branding kits toward localized material storytelling; if it scales, store-format design briefs in emerging markets could increasingly demand regional craft partnerships.
candidates.author: Dan Howarth

candidates.title: Urban-core infill for senior living, reversing suburban pattern
candidates.shift: A large continuing-care retirement community is being built in a dense Shanghai urban district rather than the low-density suburban locations typical of China's senior-living sector.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: demographic/format shift could presage urban-infill eldercare-retail adjacency models elsewhere as aging populations concentrate in city centers, reshaping nearby retail catchments and real estate mix.
candidates.evidence: Shanghai Guohua Heyuejia International Senior Living Centre sited in Taopu Smart City, an urban district, departing from the sector's suburban norm.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of eldercare real estate moving from land-cheap suburban campuses to dense urban infill; if it becomes standard, retailers near such sites would face a shifting, older, urban-core customer base and new accessibility/format requirements.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Informal social-commerce merchants moving toward AI-agent marketplaces
candidates.shift: Myanmar's secondhand and local fashion merchants, currently operating through Facebook/Viber, are the subject of a proposed AI-agent marketplace architecture to add order management and trust verification.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative and speculative: if structured platforms displace informal social commerce in emerging markets, it could eventually require physical sorting/logistics hubs for secondhand goods that don't yet exist — an absence worth watching in peripheral-geography retail.
candidates.evidence: Survey-based requirements analysis for an MCP-driven multi-agent marketplace architecture for Myanmar secondhand/local fashion merchants.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of informal social commerce professionalizing via AI tooling in a peripheral market; if secondhand/local fashion trade formalizes, it could generate demand for small-scale sorting, storage and last-mile logistics infrastructure not currently built for this category.
candidates.author: Nei Rin Zara Lwin, Kyaw Kyaw Oo, Si Thu Aung

candidates.title: Tourism demand volatility reshaping regional agri-supply-chain logic
candidates.shift: Seasonal rural tourism demand is reported to be reshaping the operational logic of regional grain supply chains that also serve farmhouse catering, farming experiences, and local souvenirs.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative cross-branch convergence: supply-chain resilience literature merging with tourism/experience economy — hints at future convergence of retail experience and last-mile agri-logistics in rural/peripheral markets.
candidates.evidence: Case study of grain industry supply chain resilience under rural tourism-driven seasonal demand volatility.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of supply chains being redesigned around experience-economy demand rather than pure logistics efficiency; if this spreads, rural retail/food supply infrastructure may need to flex for tourism seasonality alongside commodity flows.
candidates.author: Jianying Zhang, Wei Lü

candidates.title: Blockchain traceability proposed as circular-economy enabler for food
candidates.shift: A conceptual paper proposes blockchain-based traceability as the mechanism to make circular supply chains viable in the food industry — not yet deployed at scale.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if this moves from concept to deployment, it could create new packaging/reverse-logistics categories and traceability requirements for grocery retail circular loops — currently just a proposed framework.
candidates.evidence: Conceptual/framework paper on blockchain as an enabler of circular supply chains in the food industry.
candidates.source: Highlights in Science Engineering and Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of an absence — no standardized traceability/verification layer yet exists for circular food supply chains — being addressed conceptually; real deployment would require new store-level reverse-logistics and packaging-return infrastructure.
candidates.author: Xuanxi Bi

candidates.title: Absence of a 'green industrial diplomacy' framework for circular economy trade
candidates.shift: A paper argues circular economy transitions need dedicated international diplomatic/trade coordination mechanisms, which are currently fragmented across disciplines and regions.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence signal: lack of coordinated green industrial diplomacy could leave circular material sourcing for retail/construction exposed to trade friction as more countries adopt divergent circular-economy rules.
candidates.evidence: Paper framing the need for green industrial diplomacy to support circular economy transitions amid fragmented international literature/policy.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of policy infrastructure lagging behind a material-flow shift; if unresolved, circular-material sourcing for construction and retail packaging could face inconsistent cross-border rules, complicating capital and supply planning.
candidates.author: S. Sarkar, Suraj Kumar Maurya

candidates.title: News monitoring as a stand-in for missing occupational heat surveillance
candidates.shift: Researchers use online news monitoring as a sentinel tool to track occupational heat-related illness, because traditional surveillance systems undercount these events.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence signal: no standardized real-time occupational heat-tracking system exists; this could presage new compliance/insurance categories for warehouse, delivery, and outdoor retail workers exposed to rising heat.
candidates.evidence: Six-year (2020-2025) Italian study using online news monitoring as a complementary sentinel for occupational heat adverse events.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of surveillance-gap-filling via alternative data (news) instead of formal reporting; if adopted more broadly, it could pressure regulators/insurers to formalize occupational heat-exposure standards for warehouse and outdoor retail labor.
candidates.author: Giulia Ionita, Erica Mencucci, Giulia Guerri et al.

candidates.title: Wired-vs-wireless energy tradeoff for building digital infrastructure
candidates.shift: A study optimizes campus network cabling and measures device-level energy consumption, finding Wi-Fi's long-term energy footprint often exceeds wired alternatives despite convenience.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: relevant to the open 'compute?' hunt zone under utilities — in-store networks supporting sensors, cameras, and robotics may face the same wired/wireless energy tradeoff as physical AI proliferates in retail spaces.
candidates.evidence: MST-based cabling optimization and device-level energy consumption measurements on a university campus network.
candidates.source: Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli Üniversitesi İİBF Dergisi
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a build/infrastructure decision (wired vs wireless) becoming an energy and compute cost question rather than just a convenience one; as stores add more physical-AI sensors, this tradeoff could shape retrofit budgets and energy-code compliance.
candidates.author: Irmak Uzun Bayar, Ceyda CEYLAN

candidates.title: Cumulative thermal discomfort reshaping household heating priorities
candidates.shift: A new Thermal Discomfort Index captures how prolonged, cumulative cold stress — not just linear temperature response — drives household heating decisions, revealing 'constrained resignation' behavior.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: if standard heating-degree-day models understate cumulative discomfort, retail and commercial HVAC design/energy-efficiency standards built on those models may be miscalibrated for occupant comfort and energy demand.
candidates.evidence: Introduction of a cumulative Thermal Discomfort Index (TDI) in a French household energy study, published in Energy Policy.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a reframing — comfort modeling shifting from linear/degree-day metrics to cumulative-stress metrics — that could eventually change how commercial buildings, including stores, are designed and rated for occupant comfort and energy use.
candidates.author: Elisabeth Bourgeois

candidates.title: Hot-humid climate design lessons from Nigerian mixed-use high-rises
candidates.shift: A study evaluates thermal comfort performance in mixed-use high-rise buildings in Ogbomoso, Nigeria, drawing climate-responsive design implications for hot-humid urban environments.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral geography (West Africa) generating climate-adaptive mixed-use design knowledge that temperate markets facing more extreme heat may eventually need to import rather than export.
candidates.evidence: Thermal comfort evaluation study of mixed-use high-rise buildings in Ogbomoso, Southwestern Nigeria.
candidates.source: Scholarly Journal of Science and Technology Research and Development
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of the periphery setting rather than receiving a design standard: as heat events intensify globally, hot-humid climate design practices developed in West Africa could migrate into mixed-use retail/residential design elsewhere.
candidates.author: O. O. ODUNJO, Odetoye A. S., U. O. Adigun et al.

candidates.title: Buildings as standardized thermal-mass energy storage
candidates.shift: An IEA task investigates standardizing the use of thermally activated building mass as distributed energy storage/flexibility to absorb variable renewable generation.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could turn store HVAC/structural mass into a grid-flexibility asset, creating a new real-estate-utility asset class and blurring the line between construction and utility infrastructure — strange but plausible for large-footprint retail buildings.
candidates.evidence: IEA Energy Storage TCP Task 43: 'Storage for Renewables and Flexibility through Standardized Use of Building Mass.'
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a shift from buildings-as-passive-consumers to buildings-as-active-grid-assets, driven by renewable penetration; if standardized, large retail footprints could become valued partly for their thermal-storage/grid-flexibility capacity, not just floor space.
candidates.author: Alireza Afshari, Christoph Rohringer, Shady Attia

candidates.title: Historic-district zoning reform to add housing near legacy retail corridors
candidates.shift: Richmond, VA is studying how to expand housing supply and affordability within historic neighborhoods without eroding the character that makes them desirable — a live zoning/preservation tension.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: zoning reform in historic districts could reshape adjacent retail catchments and real-estate mix as these areas densify with 'missing middle' infill, a pattern other legacy retail corridors may face.
candidates.evidence: VCU Scholars Compass study on expanding housing opportunities while preserving character in Richmond's historic neighborhoods amid rising housing costs.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of zoning policy trying to reconcile preservation with density; if historic-district infill spreads, retail corridors embedded in these neighborhoods could see shifting demographics, foot traffic, and rent dynamics.
candidates.author: Jessica Russo

candidates.title: Modular construction's carbon case is more fragmented than assumed
candidates.shift: A systematic review finds evidence on whether modular/prefabricated housing genuinely reduces whole-life carbon is fragmented and context-specific, undermining a widely assumed sustainability benefit.
candidates.ai_read: Included as Trend/Context — already a live industry debate. Flags that retailers/developers betting on modular store construction for speed and ESG credit may not get the assumed carbon benefit automatically.
candidates.evidence: Systematic synthesis of Scopus-indexed studies (2012-2026) on lifecycle carbon performance of modular/prefab residential construction.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a widely-marketed construction-method benefit (modular = lower carbon) coming under empirical scrutiny; if the ambiguity holds, ESG claims tied to modular store/warehouse construction may need independent verification rather than assumption.
candidates.author: Benjamin Moral, Williams Idakwoji

candidates.title: Adaptive-reuse renovation wave in aging commercial hospitality real estate
candidates.shift: An architecture studio has renovated the interiors of a decades-old, HOK-designed hotel in Chicago, refreshing dark, dated premium spaces with light-focused redesign.
candidates.ai_read: Labeled Trend/borderline — a single named renovation project reflecting the broader, already-covered adaptive-reuse pattern in aging commercial real estate; included for context on renovation cycles applicable to retail-adjacent hospitality assets.
candidates.evidence: KTGY's renovation of 83 rooms and lounges at the Fairmont Hotel, Chicago, refreshing an HOK-designed property.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of the ongoing adaptive-reuse/renovation cycle in aging premium commercial real estate; if this pace continues, it signals steady capital flow into refreshing legacy retail-adjacent hospitality assets rather than new-build.
candidates.author: Ben Dreith

candidates.title: US-Canada tariff escalation hits building-materials and goods supply chains
candidates.shift: A 50% US tariff on many Canadian imports has taken effect as bilateral trade talks stall, directly raising costs on lumber, steel, and other goods flowing into US construction and retail supply chains.
candidates.ai_read: Labeled Trend — already a widely covered, named policy event; included for judgment given cascading consequences for store-construction material costs, cross-border freight routing, and retail goods pricing.
candidates.evidence: Reporting that a 50% tariff on many Canadian imports is now in effect after trade negotiations failed to produce an agreement.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a named, counted trade-policy shock (not a weak signal) with clear second-order effects on construction materials and retail goods costs; included at Trend classification for Kristen's calibration against genuine weak signals.
candidates.author: Phil Neuffer
